title: People within the project and people affected by it
blurb: Separate the people working within the project from the people its change affects, and explain why PRINCE2 needs both.
question: A council project is changing how bin crews plan their routes. The crews are not in the project team. Are they part of the project's 'people', and how might they contribute?

teach.body: In PRINCE2, 'people' covers those working on the project and the relationships between them, as well as those affected by it. People within the project hold roles in the defined project team: board members, the project manager, team managers, team members, assurance and support. People affected by the project do not work in that team, but the project's outputs and the change they enable alter their work, routines or responsibilities.

teach.caption: Both groups are stakeholders. Only the first group sits in the defined project team.

teach.body: A project exists to deliver change, and that change reaches into people's business-as-usual activities, routines and responsibilities. How well it lands depends on the project team's capabilities, the strength of relationships between them, and the people impacted. So PRINCE2 asks projects to involve both those with formal roles and key people who are impacted or critical to success, even if they hold no formal role.

teach.h: Sorting the people on one project
head: Person
Within or affected?
rows: Staff who will use the new system
teach.caption: Representing users does not put the senior user outside the project: the role sits on the project board.

teach.body: Saltmarsh District Council is introducing route-planning tablets for its bin crews. Project manager Grace Okafor's team includes the senior user, Depot Manager Kwame Asante, two team managers and the supplier's developers: all within the project. The 40 crew members and the call-centre staff who answer residents' queries are affected but not in the team. Grace invites crew leaders to trial the tablets and helps the depot integrate them into daily routines.

teach.text: Sample-paper trap: the executive, senior user and team managers are WITHIN the project, even though they talk to the business and represent users. The people 'affected but not in the team' are those whose work changes and who may integrate the new products into their own area.

items: 'People' covers those working on the project and those affected by it.
Within: anyone holding a role in the defined project team, including the board.
Affected: people whose work, routines or responsibilities change but who are not in the team.
Affected people may contribute by integrating new products into their area (manual 3.3.1).
Involve key people who are impacted or critical to success even without a formal role (manual 3.2.2).

summary: You can now tell people within the project (holders of project roles, including the board) from people affected by it (those whose work changes but who are outside the team). You can also explain why both matter: change only succeeds when the people it reaches adopt it.

A.q: Which group does PRINCE2's people element cover?
options: The project management team and the business layer
Those working on the project and those affected by it
The project board and the users it represents
The suppliers and their contracted team members
A.why: In PRINCE2, 'people' covers those working on the project and the relationships between them, as well as those impacted by it.

whyNot.0: The business layer is one part of the wider organization; the people element is defined by working on or being affected by the project.
whyNot.2: The board and users are included, but the definition is wider: everyone working on the project and everyone affected.
whyNot.3: Suppliers' staff may work on the project, but the people element also covers everyone the change affects.

A.q: A warehouse supervisor will not join the project team, but her shift's routines will change when the new system goes live. How does PRINCE2 describe her?
options: A person working within the project
A member of the project management team
A person affected by the project
A delegated holder of project assurance
A.why: She holds no project role, but the project changes her work, so she is a person affected by the project (and a stakeholder).

whyNot.0: People within the project hold a role in the defined project team; she does not.
whyNot.1: The project management team is made up of the defined project roles; she holds none of them.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is a role appointed by the board; nothing in the situation gives her that role.

A.q: How may people who are affected by a project, but do not work in the defined project team, contribute to it?
options: By integrating new products into their area of the organization
By approving requests for change as the delegated change authority
By setting the stage tolerances within which the PM works
By producing checkpoint reports for the project manager
A.why: The manual notes that people affected but outside the team may contribute by integrating new products into their area of the organization (3.3.1).

whyNot.1: A change authority is a role delegated by the board, so it would be part of the project, not an outside contribution.
whyNot.2: Stage tolerances are set by the project board.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports are produced by team managers, who are within the project.

B.q: Which person is WITHIN the project rather than only affected by it?
options: A customer whose ordering process will change
A call-centre agent who will answer new queries
The senior user who represents the user community
A retail manager whose store adopts the new tills
B.why: The senior user holds a role on the project board (directing level), so they are within the project even though they represent users.

whyNot.0: A customer whose process changes is affected by the project but holds no project role.
whyNot.1: The agent's work changes, but they are not in the defined project team.
whyNot.3: The store manager is affected by the change and may integrate it, but holds no project role here.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. A stakeholder may hold no formal role in the project.
2. Only people who hold a project role can be stakeholders.
3. Someone who perceives themselves to be affected is a stakeholder.
4. People affected by a project are part of the project management team.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: A stakeholder can affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves to be affected by the project (3), and key people may hold no formal role (1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: stakeholders include people with no project role.
whyNot.1: Both are false: stakeholders need not hold roles, and affected people are not automatically in the project management team.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the project management team is the set of defined project roles.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 ask projects to involve key people who are impacted by the change but hold no formal role?
options: Their sign-off replaces approval by the project board
How well change lands depends on the people it impacts
They take over from the PM once delivery begins
Their tasks are planned in the project's team plans
B.why: Change affects people's routines and responsibilities, and how well it is implemented depends on the team, its relationships and the people impacted (manual 3, 3.2.2).

whyNot.0: Their involvement does not replace the board's authority to direct the project.
whyNot.2: The project manager runs the project day to day throughout; affected people do not take over.
whyNot.3: Team plans cover work within work packages; affected people outside the team are not planned that way.

C.q: A project board member says: 'The depot staff are not in our team, so they are not our concern until handover.' Which response best reflects PRINCE2?
options: Agree, because the project ecosystem covers team members
Agree, because affected staff are the business layer's job
Disagree, because the depot staff should join the board
Disagree, because affected people must be engaged throughout
C.why: People affected by the project are part of the people element and are key to adoption; they should be identified and engaged as the project progresses, not left until handover.

whyNot.0: The people element explicitly covers people affected by the project, not just the team.
whyNot.1: The board manages the interface with the organizational ecosystem; engaging affected people is part of the project's work.
whyNot.2: Engaging affected people does not mean giving them board roles; the board represents business, user and supplier interests.

C.q: Which role is responsible for the successful handover and adoption of products into the business, and must secure ongoing commitment from the user community?
options: Executive
Project manager
Senior supplier
Senior user
C.why: The senior user is responsible for handover and adoption of products and for benefits realization after closure, securing ongoing commitment from users.

whyNot.0: The executive owns the business case and secures funding; adoption by users is the senior user's focus.
whyNot.1: The project manager runs the project day to day but does not represent the user community.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of supplied products and technical integrity.

C.q: A team manager, a customer and an executive are all connected to a project. Which statement classifies them correctly?
options: The team manager and executive are within; the customer is affected
The executive is within; the team manager and customer are affected
The team manager is within; the executive and customer are affected
All three are within, because each one is a stakeholder
C.why: Team managers (delivering) and the executive (directing) hold project roles, so they are within the project; the customer is affected by it.

whyNot.1: Team managers hold a delivering-level role, so they are within the project.
whyNot.2: The executive chairs the board and secures funding, so the executive is within the project.
whyNot.3: Being a stakeholder does not make someone part of the project team; the customer holds no role.

reteach.title: The crew and the passengers
reteach.question: On a ship being refitted while it sails, who is working on the refit and who just has to live with the changes?

blocks.body: The refit crew have jobs on the refit: they plan, direct and build. They are like people within the project. The passengers and the ship's regular staff have no refit job, but their cabins, routines and duties change. They are like people affected by the project. If they will not use the new layout, the refit fails, however well the crew worked.

blocks.text: Holding a role is the test for 'within'. Representing users, as the senior user does, still means holding a role on the board.

explain.body: Everyone holding a role in the defined project team: the project board (executive, senior users, senior suppliers), the project manager, team managers and members, and the assurance and support roles.

test.q: Which person is within the project?
options: A patient whose clinic visit will change
A supplier's finance clerk paying invoices
A resident affected by new collection days
A team manager delivering a work package
test.why: Team managers hold a delivering-level role in the defined project team.

whyNot.0: A patient is affected by the change but holds no project role.
whyNot.1: The supplier's finance clerk works for the supplier organization, not in a project role.
whyNot.2: A resident is affected by the change but is outside the project team.

explain.body: People whose activities, routines or responsibilities change because of the project, but who do not work in the defined team. They may be staff, customers or other departments. They may still contribute, for example by integrating new products into their area.

test.q: Which best describes people affected by a project but not working within it?
options: People who approve the PID on the board's behalf
People whose work changes but who hold no team role
People who supply resources under a contract
People who audit quality independently of the team
test.why: They are people whose work, routines or responsibilities change but who do not work in the defined project team.

whyNot.0: Approving the PID is the project board's decision in 'authorize the project'.
whyNot.2: Contracted suppliers provide people and resources to deliver; that is a supplier interest, not the definition of affected people.
whyNot.3: Independent quality audit describes quality assurance, a business function.

explain.body: A stakeholder is any individual, group or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceives itself to be affected by the project. So everyone within the project and everyone affected by it is a stakeholder.

test.q: Which is part of the PRINCE2 definition of a stakeholder?
options: Someone holding an approved role description
Someone named in the project's stage plan
Someone who perceives they are affected by the project
Someone who is accountable to the business layer for success
test.why: A stakeholder can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by the project (manual 3.2.2).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions belong to project roles; stakeholders include people without any role.
whyNot.1: Being named in a plan is not the test; stakeholders are defined by effect or perceived effect.
whyNot.3: Accountability to the business layer describes the project board, not stakeholders in general.

explain.body: A project's change reaches into business-as-usual routines. The team must deliver well, but benefits only come when affected people adopt the new way of working. That is why PRINCE2 involves key impacted people even when they hold no formal role.

test.q: What is the main risk of a project paying attention to its own team but not to the people it affects?
options: The products may not be adopted into daily work
The project board may lose its authority to direct
The stage plans may lose their tolerances
The project log may not be set up in time
test.why: If affected people are not engaged, the products may be delivered but not adopted, so outcomes and benefits do not follow.

whyNot.1: The board's authority comes from the business layer; it is not lost by neglecting affected people.
whyNot.2: Stage tolerances are set by the board and are not removed by poor engagement.
whyNot.3: The project log is set up in starting up and initiating a project, unrelated to engaging affected people.
